title: A heart test for bounded-below left t-exact transformations
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\Phi,\Psi:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ be triangulated functors [def-weil-triangulated-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], with specified natural shift isomorphisms $\xi_E:\Phi(E[1])\cong\Phi(E)[1]$ and $\zeta_E:\Psi(E[1])\cong\Psi(E)[1]$. Let $\eta:\Phi\to\Psi$ be a natural transformation satisfying $\zeta_E\circ\eta_{E[1]}=\eta_E[1]\circ\xi_E$ for every $E$. Assume both functors preserve every lower cohomology bound: if $H^q(M)=0$ for $q<n$, then $H^q(\Phi M)=H^q(\Psi M)=0$ for $q<n$, for every integer $n$ and every $M\in D^+(\mathcal A)$.

Let $E\in D^+(\mathcal A)$ and suppose $\eta_{H^q(E)[0]}$ is invertible for every $q\in\mathbf Z$, where $H^q(E)[0]$ means the cohomology object placed in degree zero. Then $\eta_E$ is invertible. More precisely, for every $m\in\mathbf Z$, the upper truncation inclusion $c_m:\tau_{\le m}E\to E$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] makes both $H^m(\Phi c_m)$ and $H^m(\Psi c_m)$ invertible, $\eta_{\tau_{\le m}E}$ is invertible, and naturality gives
$$H^m(\eta_E)=H^m(\Psi c_m)\circ H^m(\eta_{\tau_{\le m}E})\circ H^m(\Phi c_m)^{-1}.$$
The statement allows negative lower bounds and does not assume an upper bound on $E$ or preservation of any infinite limit by either functor.

source.place: Bounded below complexes paragraph: finite Postnikov filtration and degreewise upper-truncation comparison; Stacks derived.tex Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle) and Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), truncation triangle argument generalized from derived functors to lower-bound-preserving triangulated functors.

proof.text: Fix any integer $m$. Since $E\in D^+(\mathcal A)$, choose an integer $a_0$ with $H^q(E)=0$ for $q<a_0$, and put $a=\min(a_0,m+1)$. Then $a-1\le m$ and $H^q(E)=0$ for $q<a$. Apply finite Postnikov propagation with target $\mathcal T=D^+(\mathcal B)$, the given functors and shift comparisons, and $b=m$. Its hypothesis on $\eta_{H^q(E)[0]}$ for $a\le q\le m$ is included in our hypothesis for all $q$. Hence $\eta_{\tau_{\le m}E}$ is invertible. This also covers $m<a_0$: then $a=m+1$ and the finite interval is empty.

source.place: Tag 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category), and finite induction on the successive triangles of Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), as packaged in lem-weil-pbc-finite-postnikov-isomorphism.

proof.text: The canonical truncation triangle, with $b=m+1$, is $\tau_{\le m}E\xrightarrow{c_m}E\longrightarrow T_m\longrightarrow(\tau_{\le m}E)[1]$, where $T_m=\tau_{\ge m+1}E$ and $H^q(T_m)=0$ for $q<m+1$. Both $E$ and $T_m$ are bounded below; closure of the full bounded-below subcategory under distinguished triangles therefore puts $\tau_{\le m}E$ in it too. The triangle is thus a triangle in the domain of both functors. By the definition of triangulated functor, applying either $F=\Phi$ or $F=\Psi$ gives a distinguished triangle $F(\tau_{\le m}E)\xrightarrow{F(c_m)}F(E)\longrightarrow F(T_m)\longrightarrow F(\tau_{\le m}E)[1]$, using its specified shift comparison for the last map.

Apply the lower-bound-preservation hypothesis with $M=T_m$ and $n=m+1$. For either $F$ this gives $H^{m-1}(F(T_m))=H^m(F(T_m))=0$. The long exact cohomology sequence of the image triangle in step 2 contains the exact segment $0\longrightarrow H^m(F(\tau_{\le m}E))\xrightarrow{H^m(F(c_m))}H^m(F(E))\longrightarrow0$. Thus this middle arrow is monic and epic, and hence invertible in the abelian category $\mathcal B$. This proves the two claimed truncation-map isomorphisms, for every integer $m$.

source.place: Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), proof of (2), using only the assumed tail bound in place of (1); Tag 05RS (lemma-cohomology-homological) and Tag 0147 (definition-homological).

proof.text: Naturality at $c_m$ says $\eta_E\circ\Phi(c_m)=\Psi(c_m)\circ\eta_{\tau_{\le m}E}$. Applying the functor $H^m$ preserves composition. Right-compose the resulting equality with the inverse of $H^m(\Phi(c_m))$ from step 3. This gives exactly $H^m(\eta_E)=H^m(\Psi(c_m))\circ H^m(\eta_{\tau_{\le m}E})\circ H^m(\Phi(c_m))^{-1}$. The middle factor is invertible by step 1 and functoriality, and the outside factors by step 3, so $H^m(\eta_E)$ is invertible.

source.place: Bounded below complexes paragraph: degreewise upper-truncation comparison; naturality and composition of inverses written out here.

proof.text: The integer $m$ was arbitrary, so $\eta_E$ induces an isomorphism on every cohomology object. Both its source and target lie in $D^+(\mathcal B)$ by the stated codomains of the functors. Cohomology detection of isomorphisms in that category therefore implies that $\eta_E$ is invertible. Every comparison used a single finite upper truncation and its tail, so the argument requires neither an upper bound on $E$ nor any preservation of infinite limits.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q16-2cddb46c5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and wrote no fixes. The statement is unchanged and true; it is a generic test on D+ for triangulated functors that preserve lower cohomology bounds. Step 1 applies the reviewed finite-Postnikov node with target D+(B) and a=min(a0,m+1). This gives a-1<=m and handles the empty interval; the node's hypotheses and shift equation match the item's exactly, and it has no cycle back to the item. Step 2 takes the truncation triangle (Mathlib leaf) with b=m+1; tau<=m E lies in D+ because D+ is closed under triangles, and exact functors keep the triangle distinguished. Step 3 applies the long exact sequence (Mathlib leaf): the bound for T_m with n=m+1 kills H^{m-1} and H^m of F(T_m), so H^m(F c_m) is invertible. This is exactly the proof of Stacks 05TC(2) at derived.tex l.5497, with the assumed bound in place of 05TC(1). Step 4 is correctly elementary: naturality, apply H^m, compose with the inverse; I checked the order of the factors. Step 5 applies cohomology detection in D+(B) (Mathlib leaf Plus.isIso_iff). proof_deps equals the union of the uses. The route follows the main-20261015 sk-thm-properbasechange 'Bounded below complexes' paragraph, and the only citer (the parent's step 2) uses exactly this statement. Edge cases checked: E=0, E=A[0] with m=-5, m=a0-1, E unbounded above, a non-split E. No new nodes and no duplicates: the sbc truncation-criterion and finite-range nodes and lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-truncation-iso are about specific exchanges or Rv.
